_owner: PD (faction recruiters). Lines for the Nanotrasen and Syndicate recruiters at the trader outposts. Flavour only: no line promises a sign-up, a reward or a mechanic. A side's barbs are said to the other recruiter, so a barb's replies are in the OTHER side's voice. A conversation's replies are said by whoever the recruiter pitched to. Placeholders: {name}, {other}, {place}.

pitch: Nanotrasen is hiring! Pilots, engineers, medics, cooks.
Steady work, a pension and a uniform that fits. Think about it.
Tired of dodging pirates on your own? We have convoys for that.
Take a pamphlet. It has pictures.
Nanotrasen looks after its own. Regular pay, a real doctor, and a ship that isn't held together with tape.
Out past the yellow line nobody's coming for you. With us, somebody is.
Full medical. Dental too. Ask me about the dental.
Nanotrasen is coming to this sector. Better to be on the inside when it does.
Hot meals, clean air, paid on time.
Whole crews welcome! Bring your captain.
talk: Hi there! Ever thought about a career with Nanotrasen?
You look like someone who appreciates a steady paycheck.
We're not taking names today. Soon, though. Remember the face.
No commitment. Just have a read.
Nanotrasen has big plans for this sector. You could be part of them.
Your whole crew could fly under our colours one day. Think about that.
Don't listen to the rumours. Our medics are very good.
pamphlet: Have a read when you get a minute.
One for you. Show your captain.
The pictures are on the back.
idle: Where did I put my stapler?
Head office wants more foot traffic.
chat: Have you considered a career with Nanotrasen?
We've got openings for people like you.
Our dental plan is the envy of the sector.
How's your employer treating you? Be honest.
reply: Nanotrasen would have that fixed by now.
Sounds like you need a better employer.
Mm. Have you got a pamphlet?
We have a form for that.

conversations.opener: Ever thought about a real job?

replies: My cousin worked for you. Once.

conversations.opener: You look like Nanotrasen material, friend.

barbs.opener: Don't listen to {other}. Everyone {other} recruits ends up on a wanted poster.
replies: At least they got their pictures up.
Better a poster than a payroll number.

barbs.opener: Folks, {other}'s dental plan is a pair of pliers.
Anyone handing out flyers in a corner isn't hiring. They're hiding.
replies: Says the one with a clipboard and a quota.
Hiding from you. Can you blame us?

convoy: See that convoy? Nanotrasen runs dozens like it.
Convoys on time. That's the Nanotrasen way.
violence: I'm not paid enough for this.
cover: This never happens on Nanotrasen stations!

pitch: The Company owns your ship, your air and your name. We only want your help.
Nanotrasen pays in scrip and promises. We pay in credits.
Free crews. Free lanes. No inspections.
Take a flyer. Read it somewhere private.
They'll tell you we're pirates. Ask them who charges for oxygen.
The Company's coming out this far. You'll want friends who aren't on its payroll.
Nobody out here asked for a landlord.
Keep your ship. Keep your cargo. Keep your name off their forms.
talk: You're not Company. Good. Talk to me.
Keep your voice down. They've got ears on this concourse.
We're not recruiting. Officially. Come back when things heat up.
You fly your own ship? Good. Keep it that way.
I'm just a friend of free crews. Nothing more.
When it starts, you'll know where to find us.
It's going to get crowded out here. Pick your side early.
pamphlet: Here. Don't let the Company see it.
idle: Too many cameras on this deck.
chat: The Company treat you right? Didn't think so.
How much of your pay goes on docking fees?
We could use someone like you. Later.
Who do you think owns this station? Think harder.
Ever wonder where your fees go?

conversations.opener: Company's charging for air again. You heard?
replies: I didn't hear it from you.

conversations.opener: How long till they own your ship too?
There's work for free crews. The right kind.

barbs.opener: Your pension plan is a funeral with a logo, {other}.
replies: At least ours has a plan.

barbs.opener: Don't sign anything {other} gives you. Not even the pamphlet.
Ask {other} what happened to the last crew who read the small print.
replies: They're very happy. It says so in the newsletter.

poster: That'll give them something to read.
Let them tear that one down.
convoy: Company freight. Count the guns on it.
Another convoy. Wonder who paid for the escort.
leave: That's enough exposure for one day.
